6e22d27315.q: How should you position yourself and your background for professional Zoom calls to appear intentional and focused?
6e22d27315.a: You should be intentional about what appears behind you so people focus on you rather than distracting background elements. Frame yourself with your fingers touching the top of your head and pinky at the frame edge (the Zoom salute) to ensure proper distance from camera. Create white space on your shelves, use a peekaboo effect by partially hiding items behind plants or decor, and position interesting signature pieces like a coffee bean mug with enough white space around them so their outline is visible but not overwhelming.

04dab8512d.q: What is the Zoom salute technique and how does it improve video call framing?
04dab8512d.a: The Zoom salute is a term coined by Brenda Meller and Christopher Johnson. It involves placing your hand at the top of your forehead with your fingers touching the top of your head and your pinky finger touching the top of the frame, which helps you know you are at about the right distance from the camera. An alternative way is to hold out your hand and almost be able to touch your camera, positioned about a half inch away.

d24bc2d9c8.q: How can you organize a home office bookshelf for better appearance on video calls?
d24bc2d9c8.a: Use lower shelves for items you do not want on camera like printers, and position items on visible shelves intentionally. Add white space behind decorative items so their outlines are visible. Use greenery purchased inexpensively from Ikea to fill space, incorporate seasonal themes like pie and coffee elements in November, and use the peekaboo effect by positioning plants or decor in front of items you want partially hidden. Avoid clutter from functional office supplies like staplers, scissors, and headphones that should be tucked out of frame.

c9167a843a.q: Why should you use fake plants from Ikea in your home office video background instead of real plants?
c9167a843a.a: Real plants might die in certain home conditions. Brenda Meller is in a sunken quad-style house that gets really cold in the winter, which would kill plants. Additionally, she does not have a green thumb. Fake greenery from Ikea costs only a couple dollars each and provides the visual appeal of plants without the maintenance risk or seasonal concerns.
